items.title: Majority vote
items.description: The output is 1 when at least two of the three inputs are 1: (A and B) or (B and C) or (A and C). Three copies of a signal voted this way outvote one faulty copy.

items.title: One-bit comparator
items.description: Compares two bits: Gt is A and not B, Lt is not A and B, and Eq is 1 when neither is, that is when A equals B. The magnitude comparator builds on it.

items.title: 4-bit magnitude comparator
items.description: Four one-bit comparators, one per bit. A > B if the highest bit where they differ has A = 1: the chain of AND and OR gates passes that decision up from bit 0 to bit 3. Shown beside the Eq and LtU primitives.

items.title: Parity generator
items.description: A tree of XOR gates tells whether an 8-bit word has an odd number of 1s. Sent with the word, this parity bit lets the receiver detect a single flipped bit. Shown beside the ReduceXor primitive.

items.title: Gray code
items.description: In Gray code, neighbouring numbers differ in exactly one bit. Binary to Gray is B XOR (B shifted right by one); Gray to binary undoes it with a chain of XORs from the top bit down. The second circuit gets the original number back.

items.title: Priority encoder
items.description: Y is the number of the highest input bit that is 1, and Valid says whether any is. A chain of multiplexers passes a number up from bit 0 to bit 7; every bit that is set replaces it with its own index, so the highest one wins.

items.title: 7-segment display
items.description: A ROM holds the pattern of lit segments for each hex digit 0 to F; the seven outputs a to g are arranged like the segments of a digit. Change Digit and watch the figure change.

items.title: BCD to binary
items.description: Turns two decimal digits (tens and ones, 4 bits each) into one binary number: Tens x 10 + Ones, where Tens x 10 is Tens x 8 + Tens x 2 and multiplying by a power of two is a shift. Uses two ripple-carry adders.

items.title: Barrel shifter
items.description: Shifts A left by S places (0 to 7) in three stages: shift by 1 if bit 0 of S is set, then by 2 if bit 1 is set, then by 4 if bit 2 is set. Each stage is a word multiplexer choosing between its input and the shifted input.

items.title: Carry-lookahead adder
items.description: A ripple adder waits for each carry to pass through every bit before it. The lookahead unit computes every carry at once from the generate (A and B) and propagate (A xor B) bits: carry k+1 is 1 if bit k generates one, or a lower bit generates one and every bit above it propagates. Shown beside a 4-bit ripple adder.

items.title: 4x4 array multiplier
items.description: Multiplies like long multiplication in binary: each bit of B either keeps a copy of A or zeroes it, giving four partial products. Three rows of 4-bit ripple adders add them, each row shifted one place; one bit of the product falls out of every row.

items.title: Edge detector
items.description: A Delay remembers the input from the last tick, so 'now 1 and was 0' is a rising edge and 'now 0 and was 1' a falling edge. Each output flashes for exactly one tick; later circuits use the rising-edge detector to act once per clock period.

items.title: Shift register
items.description: Four flip-flops in a row, each one's output feeding the next one's input. On every rising clock edge the bits move one place to the right and Data enters on the left. Set Data and watch the pattern travel along the lights.

items.title: Johnson counter
items.description: A shift register whose last output is fed back, inverted, to its first input. It fills up with 1s, then with 0s, and repeats: four flip-flops give eight states, and neighbouring states differ in one bit.

items.title: Pseudo-random numbers (LFSR)
items.description: A linear-feedback shift register: each clock it shifts left and feeds in the XNOR of bits 7, 5, 4 and 3. The numbers look random but repeat after 255 steps, every 8-bit value except 255 appearing once.

items.title: Clock divider
items.description: Each bit of a binary counter changes half as often as the bit below it, so bit 0 is the clock divided by 2, bit 1 by 4, and so on. Built on the 8-bit counter from the curriculum.

items.title: Up/down counter
items.description: On every rising clock edge while Enable is 1, the register loads Q + 1 when Up is 1 and Q - 1 when Up is 0. Subtracting 1 is adding 255: the carry out of the top bit is simply dropped.

items.title: BCD counter
items.description: Two decimal digits counting 00 to 99. Each digit is a counter that goes back to 0 after Last (here 9) and then gives a one-tick Carry, which steps the next digit. Reset clears both.

items.title: Debouncer
items.description: A real button bounces between 0 and 1 for a moment when pressed. The debouncer keeps the last four samples and only changes its output when all four agree: all 1 sets the latch, all 0 resets it.

items.title: PWM generator
items.description: Pulse-width modulation: a 4-bit counter runs from 0 to 15 over and over, and the output is 1 while the count is below Duty. So the output is on for Duty out of every 16 ticks, which is how a digital pin dims a light.

items.title: Sequence detector
items.description: A finite-state machine that lights Found after the bits 1, 0, 1, 1 arrive in a row (overlaps count). Set Bit, then press Step: the state register moves to the state the table gives for the old state and the new bit. State 4 means the pattern was just seen.

items.title: Traffic light
items.description: A counter steps through ten phases, one per clock period, and a ROM turns each phase into lights: north-south green for four phases, yellow for one, then the same for east-west while north-south is red. The counter is the BCD counter's digit with Last = 9.

items.title: Stopwatch
items.description: Three digit counters in a chain count tenths, seconds and tens of seconds (up to 59.9); a digit's carry steps the next one. Run starts and stops counting, Reset clears the time. One clock period is a tenth.
